answer: The grocer stamps his weights at the guild and enters every weighing in his stamp book against the customer who bought. A echo weight bought from a pedlar fails the book: at the vertex of the stamp the brass must match the grocer's own set, and a pedlar's weight cheats by an ounce. Forging a weighing means hiring a grocer, buying false brass and paying 4,300, and the lotus entry in the stamp book is read at every assize, so goods whose weighing was never entered are seized.
